call.note: the callee at 0x3cc6500 IS an FDE start (302 bytes, .eh_frame+0x0050dd20, CIE 0x002dc714, a different CIE from the window's 0x00000000), but its body is excluded here; only the call encoding and the FDE record are retained, so no claim about what it computes is made

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase

function.padding_note: thirteen int3 bytes (0xcc) at [0x3cbf023, 0x3cbf030) pad the window to the next FDE at 0x3cbf030

validated_caller_fdes.note: the caller disassembly from its FDE start shows the e8 call to the window at 0x3cbfa87 as an instruction start; the caller passes a stack address (lea rdi, [rsp+0x40]) and, after the call, jumps to a continuation inside its own FDE; the caller role beyond the call site is not established

args.note: the callee arguments are identical on every attempt: rdi is the struct pointer, rsi is the fixed address 0x1ea44d (lea r14, [rip-0x3ad4b8f]), and rdx is the stack slot at [rsp+8] whose first qword is the struct+0x20 address (lea r13, [rdi+0x20]) and whose second qword is the global qword at 0x576e780 (mov rbp, [rip+0x1aaf7ab]). What the fixed address, the global, and the slot mean is not established, so no claim about them is made beyond the addresses and the slot layout.
args.rdi: struct pointer (entry rdi, saved in rbx)
args.rdx: stack slot at [rsp+8]: slot[0] = struct+0x20 address, slot[1] = qword at 0x576e780

edges.note: zero attempts: the window returns 0 without calling anything (je to the xor-eax path before the loop)
one attempt, callee returns 0: the counter decrements to 0, the loop exits, the window returns 0
one attempt, callee returns nonzero: the jne path returns that value immediately
two attempts, first returns 0, second returns nonzero: the window returns the second value
three attempts, all return 0: the counter exhausts, the window returns 0
three attempts, first two return 0, third returns nonzero: the window returns the third value
early exit: the first attempt returns nonzero, so the second attempt never happens and later callee results are never consumed
five attempts, all return 0: the window returns 0 after exactly five calls

rule.formula: attempts = the qword at [rdi+0x18]; if attempts == 0, return 0 without calling; else repeat up to attempts times: call 0x3cc6500 with rdi = struct pointer, rsi = 0x1ea44d, rdx = stack slot (slot[0] = struct+0x20 address, slot[1] = qword at 0x576e780); if the callee result is nonzero, return it at once; if it is zero, decrement attempts and repeat while attempts != 0; if every attempt returns 0, return 0
rule.formula_note: the loop re-sets the slot contents and the three callee arguments on every iteration from loop-invariant values, so every attempt is made with identical arguments. The callee result convention (nonzero terminates, zero retries) follows directly from the test/jne branch; what the callee computes, and what its nonzero values mean, is excluded with the callee body. The window writes nothing into the struct itself: the only stores are the two slot qwords on the stack. The attempts count is a qword; the dec/jne counter means exactly N calls happen when all N results are zero.
rule.inputs: struct pointer (rdi; attempts qword at +0x18, slot base address at +0x20), callee results (one u64 per attempt)
